name: Surgical Robotics and AI
blurb: New robotic surgery systems and the AI in them.
title: Surgical Robotics and AI
answer: Robotic surgery is opening up beyond one dominant platform: Medtronic's Hugo and CMR Surgical's Versius Plus both received FDA clearance in December 2025. AI features in surgery so far mostly assist, such as video analysis and guidance, rather than acting autonomously.

reading.body:
Two new surgical robot platforms cleared the FDA in December 2025, Medtronic's Hugo and CMR Surgical's Versius Plus, ending a period when one system dominated the market. The AI in these systems assists rather than operates: video analysis and guidance, not autonomous action.

The pattern is a market opening at the platform layer before the intelligence layer matures. Clearance of two competing systems matters less for what they do today than for the installed base they begin building. Each procedure a robot performs generates structured video and motion data, and that corpus is the raw material any future surgical AI would train on. The company that accumulates the most procedures holds the most valuable dataset, which is why platform competition and AI capability are linked even while the AI itself stays assistive.

For AI specifically, this is a reminder that capability in regulated fields follows hardware deployment, not the reverse. A surgical model cannot be trained on operations that were never recorded, and operations are recorded only where a robot is installed and cleared. Compute and model progress are necessary but not sufficient here, because the binding constraint is clinical clearance and adoption, not processing power. Nothing in this data speaks to data center capacity, power draw, or training compute, and surgical robotics is not a meaningful driver of any of them.

What the data does not cover is how many units either company has placed, what either system's AI actually does in the operating room, or whether the two clearances are for the same procedures. It records two regulatory events and a general characterization of AI's role. It does not establish that either platform's data is being used to train anything.

sections.body: Competition among platforms will drive down robot costs; the data each system captures is the longer term AI asset.
